status: APPROVED BY THE OWNER, 2026-11-13, as part of the placement criteria set drafted by Task 7 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-12-agent-pcb-place-and-route-phase-1.md and independently reviewed before it reached him. He was put the one deliberate judgement in the set - the extent of U1's zone in floorplan-intent.json - and ruled "loosen to 80%. The chip should be near the middle of the drawing, but perfect alignment is not critical". Nothing in THIS file changed under that ruling; it is approved as reviewed. READ `reading_the_enforced_by_field` BEFORE RELYING ON ANY RULE HERE: five of the seven carry `none-in-phase-1`, so approval of this file is not a claim that anything checks each rule in it. Changing it now invalidates every run made under it.
derived_from: circuits/pt2399-core/pt2399-core.ts (the circuit model), docs/standards/pcbway-fab-rules.md (every fabrication value), and the installed KiCad footprint library (every footprint dimension quoted below). NOT from the board's current part positions: those were written by the headless update tool on a mechanical 15 mm grid and are not a floorplan.
reading_the_enforced_by_field: Each rule names the mechanism that can make it fail. Where that field says `none-in-phase-1`, NOTHING CHECKS THE RULE YET and it must not be read as checked. Phase 1 is a probe; the spec's facility, with check-intent carrying the repository-side rules, is Phase 2.

input_to_output.what: INPUT copper and OUTPUT copper must not run together anywhere on the board.
input_to_output.why: Both nets land on J1, and the circuit between them has gain and a regeneration path through Net-(C12-Pad1). Coupling from the output back into the input is the failure this rule exists to prevent.
input_to_output.min_gap_derivation: This floor is read off the board's own worst case rather than chosen. The model puts OUTPUT on J1 pin 4 and INPUT on J1 pin 5 - ADJACENT pins. Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm:PinHeader_1x05_P2.54mm_Vertical places them 2.54 mm apart centre to centre with 1.7 mm pads, so 0.84 mm of copper gap at the header is forced by the schematic and the footprint and cannot be improved by any placement or routing decision. The rule is therefore: nowhere ELSE may the two nets come closer than they already are at J1's own pads. A smaller number would permit the rest of the board to be worse than the one place that cannot be fixed.
input_to_output.measure: The closest input/output copper gap on the routed candidate, which the spec already lists among the route step's recorded metrics.
input_to_output.ranking: Among candidates that pass, largest gap first - the spec's ranking rule for this board. The floor refuses; the ranking chooses.
input_to_output.no_upper_criterion_authored: There is no 'good' gap written here. Nothing in this repository establishes a crosstalk clearance for audio at these impedances, and an agent may not author the acceptance criteria for the artifact it is producing. The gap is measured, ranked, and ruled on by the owner on the render.
input_to_output.kicad_dru_decision: NO custom .kicad_dru isolation rule is written for this board, and the reason is the measurement above rather than a judgement that it does not matter. An UNCONDITIONED net-to-net clearance rule can only add something if it demands more than the project's global 0.25 mm copper clearance, and it cannot demand more than 0.84 mm without rejecting J1's own pads - the schematic puts INPUT and OUTPUT on adjacent header pins and the schematic is authoritative here. So its usable window is 0.25 to 0.84 mm, and the tightest input-to-output approach on the board sits at the top of it, at the header, where no rule can move it. A rule CONDITIONED to exempt the pads is available - KiCad takes a condition such as `A.Type != 'Pad'` - and would escape that ceiling, which is why the ceiling is not the whole argument and this clause used to overstate it. The argument that does carry: either form buys a check, a cost and a new way to fail for a constraint that placement already expresses, and neither moves the binding approach at the connector. The separation that matters on this board is a PLACEMENT property - the ordering rule below keeps the two paths at opposite ends with the DIP between them - and that is where it is expressed. tests/pcb/placement-intent-geometry.test.ts re-derives the 0.84 mm and the pin adjacency on every run, so if either changes, this decision fails rather than going stale.
input_to_output.enforced_by: none-in-phase-1 for the floor. The route step records the metric (spec Phase 1 metrics); Task 10 compares it against this floor by reading it. Phase 2's check-intent is where it becomes a gate.

part_to_part.what: No two parts' courtyards may come closer than 2.0 mm anywhere on the board.
part_to_part.why: THE OWNER BUILDS THIS BOARD BY HAND. His directive, 2026-11-13, verbatim: "remember that I have fingers, so I need enough room between parts to use my fingers. I'm not a pick and place machine" - and his ruling on the figure, same day: "Use 2mm min spacing and increase the board size to 150mm x 100mm". This is an assembly constraint, not an electrical one, and it is HIS number. An agent may not author it, because the placement is what it grades.
part_to_part.he_had_already_said_this_and_the_pcb_pat: The same directive is recorded in `lib/stripboard/seed-area.ts` in nearly the same words - "I try to cluster related parts, AND I try to give myself room to work. I have actual fingers-I'm not a pick and place machine" - with his priority beside it: "Clustering is nice, but secondary to ease of assembly." It was enforced for stripboard and NEVER CARRIED ACROSS to the PCB path, which is why he had to say it twice. The lesson is not about this number: a directive recorded against one output class does not reach another one by itself, and nothing in this repository checked for that.
part_to_part.and_the_stripboard_tolerance_does_not_tr: His stripboard boards mostly leave parts ADJACENT - 14 of 16 parts on `transistor-preamp-feedback` touch their nearest neighbour - and `seed-area.ts` therefore makes crowding a preference rather than a refusal. That reasoning does NOT carry to a fabricated board, by his own words about why: "Don't worry about body collisions on the stripboard. It's extremely flexible." A stripboard part can be jostled aside; a drilled hole cannot. So the PCB gets a refusal where stripboard gets a tier.
part_to_part.what_the_board_had_before_this_rule: 0.25 mm, AND NOBODY CHOSE IT. The placer's `--clearance` flag means 'min courtyard gap' but defaults to the board's Default net-class COPPER clearance, so part spacing was silently inheriting a copper-to-copper rule. Measured on a clean 65 x 50 seed before the ruling: tightest pair 0.318 mm courtyard to courtyard, about 0.8 mm body to body, with 6 of 24 parts inside 0.5 mm of a neighbour. A number that arrives by inheritance from an unrelated rule is the shape of defect this clause exists to name.
part_to_part.measured_cost_of_the_ruling: Seeds 0-7 at 2.0 mm: on the owner's 150 x 100 board, 3 clean of 8, every failure a single named cap (C1 or C2, the known structural pair), eight decap seats on every run, and no `legality`, `zone_containment`, `edge_connector` or unseated part - so it meets the Task 8 evidence bar on both clauses. On the earlier candidate rectangles 2.0 mm was tighter than they could take: 65 x 50 gave 0 clean of 8 and brought a THIRD cap (C4) into the failures, 50 x 80 gave 3 of 8. Verified on a clean 150 x 100 seed, the achieved minimum gap is exactly 2.000 mm with nothing below it. At 3.0 mm no rectangle produces a clean seed and J1 can no longer make its edge setback, so 2.0 mm sits inside the feasible range rather than at its edge.
part_to_part.the_rule_it_trades_against: `floorplan-intent.json` `decaps.max_distance_mm` of 10.0 mm. Spreading parts apart pushes the bypass caps away from U1, so these two rules pull in opposite directions and the decap rule is what fails first as spacing rises. Both are the owner's; neither is an agent's to relax to make the other reachable.
part_to_part.enforced_by: TWO mechanisms at one number, deliberately, the same pattern Task 8 uses for the mounting envelope. (1) The placer: `--clearance 2.0` on `place_seed.py`, `place_portfolio.py` and `place_optimize.py`, which is a hard veto on candidate positions rather than a cost term. (2) KiCad DRC: a `(constraint courtyard_clearance (min 2mm))` custom design rule, so the shipped board is checkable independently of the placer that produced it. BOTH ARE NOW WIRED UP, and the second is MEASURED rather than read from documentation: the constraint reports as `courtyards_overlap` at error severity, a type already in `tools/pcb/drc-report.ts`'s REQUIRED_ACTIVE_CHECKS, so nothing was widened to admit it. `circuits/pt2399-core/pt2399-core.kicad_dru` carries the rule, is generated from the `min_gap_mm` above, and is compared BY CONTENT as a prerequisite of every DRC make target, refusing when missing or loosened. Driven in both directions: clean at 2 mm, 24 violations naming the rule at 2.5 mm. THE MINIMUM GAP ON THE DELIVERED BOARD IS NOT TRANSCRIBED HERE, and that is a correction: this clause carried "2.0000 mm, zero pairs below" with NO METHOD NAMED, and a re-reviewer could not reproduce it because KiCad's own `courtyard_clearance` measure reports about 2.0100 mm. Both figures are right for their own measure - 2.0000 mm is the minimum separation of axis-aligned courtyard BOUNDING BOXES, which enclose the courtyard and therefore give a lower bound, while KiCad compares the courtyard outlines themselves - so the number was never wrong, only unattributable, which in a criteria file is the same problem. **A figure here is a transcription with a date on it; the authority is whatever re-runs the measurement.** For KiCad's measure that is `tests/pcb/courtyard-rule.test.ts` and `make drc-unrouted-pt2399-core`, which fail if the floor stops being met rather than reporting a number nobody can reproduce. CORRECTED 2026-11-13: this clause read "NEITHER IS WIRED UP YET" after both had been. Its sibling in floorplan-intent.json went stale the same way and was corrected in the same commit after the Task 8 re-review found that one - the lesson being that a "not yet" written into a criteria file is a claim with an expiry date, and the agent that wires the mechanism up is the one that has to come back for the sentence. WHAT IS STILL NOT CHECKED: `tools/pcb/fab-standard.ts` reads no `.kicad_dru` at all, so this board's rule is gated by a make prerequisite and by `tests/pcb/courtyard-rule.test.ts`, and a second board gaining its own rule would get neither - recorded in that file's own "WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT CHECK" section and deliberately not solved, there being no second board. `make check` does not run either, so the unconditional home of this guard is the test.

signal_path.what: The blocks lie along the signal path in this order, pairwise non-overlapping: input_path, lpf1_node, delay_ic, lpf2_regen_node, output_path.
signal_path.why: This is a fact of the netlist, not a preference. INPUT enters C7, through R3 into the LPF1 summing node Net-(C8-Pad2), through R1 into U1 pin 16; the delayed signal leaves U1 pin 14 into the regeneration node Net-(C12-Pad1) and, through R5, into Net-(C10-Pad1) and out of C10 to OUTPUT. Laying the blocks along that chain is also what holds the input and output paths apart, with the DIP between them, so this rule and separation.input_to_output are two statements of one arrangement.
signal_path.attached_to_delay_ic_why: These three blocks have no position in the chain: every member connects to a U1 pin and to GND or to a second U1 pin, so they belong against the IC rather than anywhere along the path.
signal_path.enforced_by: none-in-phase-1, and the chain is PARTLY implied rather than checked. `anchors.delay_ic` pins the middle of it, and the seeder then places everything else at its connectivity centroid, which tends to lay the chain out because the chain is what the netlist says - but nothing measures the ORDER, and a seed that folded the input path round next to the output path would grade clean. That is the gap to close in Phase 2's check-intent, and in the meantime it is what the owner is looking at on the render.

decoupling_to_u1.what: Every cap sharing a non-ground net with U1 sits within 10.0 mm of U1.
decoupling_to_u1.measured_as: cap centroid to U1's pad bounding box, which is what the engine's decap tether measures.
decoupling_to_u1.derivation: 10.0 mm is a feasibility bound, not a taste figure, and every number in it is re-derived by tests/pcb/placement-intent-geometry.test.ts rather than written down here. From the installed library: U1's courtyard extends 1.055 mm beyond its pad field on each long side and 1.520 mm on each short side, and the narrowest courtyard dimension of a part on this board is 3.000 mm. A part laid broadside against the IC therefore centres 2.555 mm from the pad field on a long side, and a second row of such parts begins at 5.555 mm on a long side and 6.020 mm on a short one. An earlier draft of this clause said 'about 5.8 mm', which was a hand-rounded figure between those two and is now computed; nothing load-bearing turned on it, because 10.0 clears both. Nine caps and the six resistors that land on a U1 pin (R1, R2, R5, R6, R7 and R8) all want a place against U1's courtyard perimeter, so the limit has to admit a second row; 10.0 mm does, with margin, while still failing a cap parked across the board.
decoupling_to_u1.enforced_by: floorplan-intent.json `decaps.max_distance_mm`, graded by the engine's `decap_distance` rule at error severity. Its `search_radius_mm` is 100.0 and is not a second limit - see that file's context.
decoupling_to_u1.least_certain: This is the number in this file I am least able to defend as THE value rather than A value. It is bounded below by what the geometry allows and above by what would be vacuous, and the owner may reasonably move it inside that range.

first_row_caps_UNSOURCED_NOTE_NOT_A_RULE.status: NOT A CRITERION. Nothing may grade a placement against this entry, and it carries no membership list on purpose. It is kept in this file, relabelled, rather than deleted, because the reasoning that refuted it is the useful part.
first_row_caps_UNSOURCED_NOTE_NOT_A_RULE.the_note: A cap that serves a PT2399 pin directly arguably belongs in the FIRST row of parts against U1 rather than the second - about 5.0 mm rather than 10.0 mm, measured as `decoupling_to_u1` measures. The arithmetic for that threshold is sound: a 6.8 mm circular courtyard centres at 1.055 + 3.4 = 4.46 mm from U1's pad field, and the second row starts above 5.5 mm, so 5.0 admits the first and excludes the second.
first_row_caps_UNSOURCED_NOTE_NOT_A_RULE.why_it_was_demoted: It was drafted as a rule with a `binds` list of C3, C4, C5, C6, C11, C13 and C14, and that list was INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT in a way that gives the premise away. It EXCLUDED C1, the 0.1 uF local supply bypass on U1 pin 1 - the one part on this board where lead length is conventionally held to matter most - while INCLUDING C3, the 47 uF reference reservoir, which this file's own earlier warning called the least sensitive to lead length and nominated as the first to relax. A rule that puts the least lead-sensitive part in the first row and leaves the most lead-sensitive one out of it is not a derivation; it is an unsourced judgement about a part. The independent reviewer found the inversion; the drafter had suspected the premise and could not name why.
first_row_caps_UNSOURCED_NOTE_NOT_A_RULE.what_would_settle_it: A PT2399 datasheet statement, or the owner's own judgement, about which of its pins need a bypass within one row. Neither the drafter nor the reviewer has that authority, and neither authored a membership list. Until then the board-wide 10.0 mm limit in `decoupling_to_u1` is the only distance anything grades against.
first_row_caps_UNSOURCED_NOTE_NOT_A_RULE.and_the_probe_says_it_would_have_failed_: Across the reviewer's sixteen seeding runs, C3 landed between 10.58 and 16.77 mm in every run that named it. Had this gone forward as a rule at 5.0 mm it would have blocked every seed, and the pressure would then have been to relax the number rather than to question the premise.
first_row_caps_UNSOURCED_NOTE_NOT_A_RULE.enforced_by: nothing, by design. The engine carries ONE decap distance for the whole board and cannot express a tighter subset even if this were a rule.

node_compactness.what: Each filter node is compact - lpf1_node around U1 pins 15 and 16, lpf2_regen_node around pins 12, 13 and 14, output_path around pin 14.
node_compactness.why: Each of these nodes is a high-impedance summing point (10K to 15K series resistors into a few nF) and its area is its antenna.
node_compactness.why_no_number: Deliberately not authored. Nothing in this repository establishes a span for a node of this impedance, and this project's rule is to refuse rather than guess; an empty criterion that says so beats a general one that quietly accepts an invented figure. What does constrain these blocks is their membership in floorplan-intent.json, the ordering rule above, and `decoupling_to_u1` - which reaches the four feedback caps C6, C11, C13 and C14 because each shares a non-ground net with U1. If the owner wants a span, he sets it on the render.
node_compactness.enforced_by: none-in-phase-1, and nothing is claimed for it.

delay_ic.what: U1 is anchored in the MIDDLE of the board, and it is the one block whose region this intent declares.
delay_ic.why: Two reasons that happen to agree. Electrically, `ordering.signal_path` below puts the DIP in the middle of the chain and every other block hangs off one of its pins, so the middle is where the circuit puts it. Mechanically, the seeder places a block early only if that block carries a region, and its decap stage seats a cap only against a supply pin of an already-placed IC - so without this anchor `proximity.decoupling_to_u1`, the only rule here that anything enforces, is unreachable. Measured: zero clean seeds in sixteen runs without it.
delay_ic.the_region_itself_is_not_here: It is in floorplan-intent.json `context.outline_derivation.zones.delay_ic`, as a fraction of the outline rather than a rectangle, with the dependency it carries and the smallest outline it fits stated beside it. One place, so the fraction cannot drift between two files.
delay_ic.enforced_by: floorplan-intent.json `blocks[delay_ic].zone` once resolved, graded by the engine's `zone_containment` rule at error severity, and aimed at by the seeder's own zone stage.

header.what: J1 is anchored on a LONG edge of the final rectangular outline, not overhanging it, with its courtyard no more than 2.5 mm from that edge, and it is locked in the board file.
header.why_a_long_edge: The spec's decision for this board. J1 is 13.70 mm of courtyard along its pin row; the long edge is where it fits without eating into a corner the mounting holes need.
header.max_setback_derivation: Below the 3.000 mm narrowest courtyard dimension of any footprint this circuit places, so nothing on this board can be placed between the header and the edge; above the fabrication standard's 0.5 mm copper-to-edge floor, so the header's own pads have room. See floorplan-intent.json for the same derivation beside the value the grader reads.
header.which_compass_edge: DERIVED, not deferred, and the earlier draft of this file was wrong to defer it. The engine states an edge as north/south/east/west, which is only meaningful once the outline has an aspect - so the rule is `the long edge`, and floorplan-intent.json `context.outline_derivation.header_edge` turns it into a compass edge from the outline's own aspect (`south` when at least as wide as tall, `east` otherwise, a tie broken once rather than per run). Leaving it out is worse than leaving it unenforced: the seeder refuses to seat an entry with no edge and says so, while the grader enforces the setback regardless, so the criterion then passed or failed on where the connectivity centroid happened to land - measured at 28.07 mm against the 2.50 mm limit on one outline and a pass by accident on another.
header.enforced_by: floorplan-intent.json `edge_connectors[J1]` (setback and overhang, error severity) and `must_lock` (locked, error severity), BOTH ON THE RESOLVED INTENT. That qualifier is load-bearing and the earlier draft of this file overstated it: those two are enforced by the GRADE either way, but the SEEDER only aims at the seat once the compass edge is present, which is what resolution supplies. On the approved file alone the setback is checked and unaimed, which is the state this fix removed.

mounting_holes.what: Four mounting holes, one near each corner of the rectangular outline, each centred 4.0 mm in from BOTH of the two edges its corner is formed by.
mounting_holes.approved_as_a_rule_not_as_coordinates: Task 8 moves the board edge and therefore the corners, so any literal coordinate approved now would be stale by the time Task 8 Step 3 regrades against it - and the regrade would then check the wrong keepouts while reporting a pass. What is put forward for approval is the invariant below. Task 8 computes the four coordinates from the FINAL outline and this rule and writes them into floorplan-intent.json `keepouts`.
mounting_holes.hole_source: A standard M3 screw in the standard 3.2 mm clearance hole - the owner's instruction of 2026-11-13, recorded verbatim in docs/known-gaps.md G311. MountingHole:MountingHole_3.2mm_M3 is exactly this hole, non-plated.
mounting_holes.envelope_source: The outside diameter of an M3 flat washer, DIN 125 Type A / ISO 7089 - 3.2 mm inside, 7.0 mm outside. No copper, part or silkscreen may sit under the washer. Two neighbours to avoid when sourcing: DIN 433 / ISO 7092 is the small series at 6.0 mm OD and DIN 9021 is the large series at 9.0 mm OD; fitting either changes this number.

centre_inset_parts.geometric_floor_is: The washer's radius. Below this the washer overhangs the board. Hard.
centre_inset_parts.design_margin_is: A design margin for board-outline routing tolerance, which is commonly around plus or minus 0.2 mm. Soft, and this plan's own.
centre_inset_parts.do_not_cite_the_margin_as_a_vendor_rule: The 0.5 mm is NOT the fabrication standard's copper-to-edge clearance, although it happens to share the value. Copper-to-edge governs copper against the board edge and is enforced globally by DRC; this envelope is a keepout and not copper, so the two do not stack. It is a margin this plan chose, and it is the one number in this rule that could reasonably be argued down to the 3.5 mm floor.

mounting_holes.modelled_by_why: KiCad's drill-clearance rules measure the hole, and the hole is 3.2 mm while the thing that must stay clear is the 7.0 mm washer. Task 8 Step 4 carries the two DRC mechanisms that enforce this - a copper-only Rule Area at 7.0 mm, and `courtyards_overlap` against a PROJECT-LOCAL footprint derived from MountingHole:MountingHole_3.2mm_M3 with its courtyard changed from the stock 6.9 mm to 7.0 mm, drill and non-plated attribute untouched. The stock 6.9 mm was measured from the installed library on 2026-11-13 and again while drafting this file.
mounting_holes.must_lock: Task 8 adds the four references to floorplan-intent.json `must_lock` in the same change that places them. They are not there now because a must_lock pattern matching no footprint is itself a violation, and the intent would then fail for bookkeeping rather than for the board.
mounting_holes.enforced_by: none-in-phase-1 while the holes do not exist. After Task 8: floorplan-intent.json `keepouts` (grader) and KiCad DRC's `items_not_allowed`, `courtyards_overlap` and `missing_courtyard`, all at error severity per docs/standards/pcbway-fab-rules.md.
